volunteering.description:
Ladies' Night at Graham Crackers Comics in downtown Chicago was founded by Hannah K Chapman in January 2012.  The first Wednesday of every month you can find a bevvy of ladies discussing comic books, video games, movies, fantasy, science fiction, zines...a little bit of everything.  We don't always agree, but we work hard to make it a welcoming space and a big part of that is encouraging our creative members with projects like our anthology.  

Since 2013, we have produced a self-published, completely volunteer run anthology every single year.  All of the participants are women or nonbinary and many of them have never made a comic before.  Editors work closely with creative teams that we assign to create between 8 and 12 stories every volume, each of them 4 to 6 pages.  Our creators have gone on to have jobs like storyboarding for major animation studios as well as getting full-time jobs writing or drawing comics, and we couldn't be prouder of the community we've created.

Whether you’re a hardcore fan, a casual gamer or a newbie who can’t tell Klingon from Quenya, all are welcome! We create fun, inclusive, welcoming spaces that are open to nerds from all walks of life and all levels of fandom – neither abusive language nor harassment of any kind are tolerated. If this description doesn’t appeal to you, as a wise old Jedi once said, “These aren’t the droids you’re looking for.”

The Chicago Nerd Social Club hosts a number of nerd-friendly events. Some are purely social: casual get-togethers at a bar, trips to the movies, gaming nights. Others are informational in nature: local museum outings, introductions to new technologies, and comic book swap nights.

headline: Manager, Employer Brand and Marketing
about: With a background in Marketing and Public Relations, Matt came to Deloitte’s Los Angeles office in 2007 to work in the firm's Creative Services group. While in Creative Services he assisted with graphic design and communications pieces for Marketing and Business Development, Talent, and other cross-functional projects. In 2010, he transitioned into Talent Acquisition in Los Angeles, where he focused on Audit campus recruiting, Japanese and Korean Service group recruiting, and served as the Recruiting Diversity Ambassador for the West region. He transferred to Chicago with Deloitte and since that time has focused on intern and entry level hiring for the Deloitte Chicago Tax practice, the largest Tax practice in the country. He also helped to lead Deloitte's experienced hire recruiting efforts for Master of Law (LLM) candidates in 2014.  Matt moved into Deloitte's Talent Strategy and Innovation team in 2015, where he focused on leading teams of recruiters in planning national recruiting events for Deloitte, such as the firm's national internship conferences and alternative spring break recruiting programs. As a part of that role he also managed relationships with several of Deloitte's non-profit partners, including United Way, Teach for America, and City Year. headline: Associate Creative Director | Brand Marketing + Culture | Visual Storytelling + Illustration | Deloitte Consulting
about:
Hi, it’s great to e-meet you. I come from a product graphic design background, I began my career at Motorola synthesizing global trends, drawing patterns, designing keyboards, and experimenting with 3D textures. 

I then scaled my product knowledge from mobile phones to laundry, fridges, ovens, and small kitchen appliances at Whirlpool. This role challenged me to think big, in a multitude of ways, considering various global and cultural differences, take into account product variation across multiple brands, and problem-solving, to turn production challenges into solutions through the unique application of graphics, patterns, materials, and finishes. Our focus was always centered around the consumer and simplifying complexity. 

As a manager at Deloitte, I’ve expanded my design focus to include, digital marketing, and people. I have the privilege of helping our ecosystems and alliances practice design creative go-to-market materials and campaigns to help promote and communicate industry-leading business solutions for our clients. 

I love illustration, design, typography, home renovations, food, and travel. I'm an admirer of fashion and interior design. I'm an extrovert and a very curious person. I enjoy reading self-help books and dabbling in art projects and local adventures with my two daughters.

Cultivated relationships and teams to find new opportunities to help drive impact. headline: Partner, National Leader (Supply Chain), Business Model Optimization, Deloitte Tax LLP
about:
I'm the National Leader (Supply Chain) within Deloitte's Business Model Optimization (BMO) pratice.  Our BMO practice focuses on creating value through structuring a company's supply chain functions and intellectual property in a tax efficient mannner.  Over the past 15 years I have helped many clients realign their supply chains in both Europe and Asia creating tax efficient structures utilizing principal or central entrepreneur companies located in Switzerland, Ireland, Singapore and other jurisdictions.  These tax efficient structures typically involve the conversion of local sales companies into stripped or limited risk distributors and buy-sell manufacturing companies into toll or contract manufacturers operating under the direction of the European or Asian principal company.  Many of these projects involved reviewing the optimal location to hold the company's intellectual property (IP) and structuring the transfer of such IP.

Specialties: Establishing tax efficient supply chain strucures in both Europe and Asia while tax optimizing the ownership of intellectual property.

My group recorded the closing price of each stock every Wednesday for the period starting on Jan. 3, 2018 and ending Wednesday, June 27, 2018. My group also recorded the level of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) and the S&P 500 index on each of those dates. We calculated the value of each portfolio on each date, created an index of portfolio value,  calculated the weighted average betas of each.
In the end, my group compared the performance of the portfolios to that of the two indexes we tracked over the period to determine whether we were adequately compensated for the risks we took.

projects.associatedWith: Associated with Transparency Market Research Pvt. Ltd.
projects.description:
U.K. Insect Repellent Market: Snapshot

Thanks to the rising demand for highly efficient insecticides containing natural ingredients, the U.K. market for insect repellents is expected to witness substantial growth over the next few years. Manufacturers of these repellants are prompted to increase their research activities to develop innovative products, which are highly effective yet cost competent.

Insect repellent on skin products are sold through different distribution channels such as supermarkets, online stores, and convenience stores. The increase in the availability of products in convenience stores, supermarkets and online stores are promoting growth of the insect repellent market in the U.K. Manufacturers also sell these products through their websites. Moreover, many companies enter into joint venture agreements with different online stores in order to sell insect repellent on skin products through their websites. The impact of this driver is medium at present, but is expected to become high in the near future.

The U.K. market for insect repellents, which stood at US$ 66.4 mn in 2016, is anticipated to increase at a healthy CAGR of 4.90% during the period from 2017 to 2025, expanding the opportunity in this market to US$100.0 mn by the end of 2024.

Aerosol Sprays to Witness Strong Demand

Predominantly, insect repellents are of two types, body worn and non-body worn. The demand for non-body worn insect repellent is much higher than their body worn counterparts. Coils, mats and sheets, electric/liquid vaporizers, and aerosol sprays are the most preferred insecticides among consumers in the U.K. Among these, the demand for aerosol is significantly higher. Aerosol cans are used to kill or repel different insects including mosquitoes, and cockroaches among others. These sprays are not meant for direct application on the skin unlike body worn aerosol sprays. Aerosol cans are tightly sealed and do not leak or spill.

projects.description:
Global Licorice Extract Market: Snapshot

Of late, the global licorice extracts market is witnessing a stable progress, thanks to the growing demand for pharmaceutical products, herbal medicines, and various other health products among people across the world. The increasing uptake of natural ingredients in medical supplements, together with the rising inclination of consumers towards sugar-free products, boosted by the upswing in the consumer consciousness towards health and fitness, is fueling the demand for licorice extracts, reflecting greatly on this market.

Currently, the market players are focusing aggressively on research and development activities to develop new products in order to satisfy the swelling demand for sugar-free products, as the rising prevalence of diabetes and obesity has increased the concerns of consumers over the high intake of sugar. This, as a result, is expected to benefit the sales of licorice extracts in the years to come. Apart from this, the opportunities generated by the advent of herbal medicines in developed regions are also projected to reflect greatly on the market for licorice extracts, globally. The overall opportunity in this market, which stood at US$1.70 bn in 2016, is anticipated to reach US$2.3 bn by 2025, expanding at a CAGR of 4.0% between 2017 and 2025.

Asia Pacific to Continue Leading Global Licorice Extracts Market

Geographically, the worldwide market for licorice extracts has been categorized into the Middle East and Africa, Europe, North America, Latin America, and Asia Pacific. Driven by China, India, and Japan, Asia Pacific dominated the global market in 2016 with a share of more than 32%. Analysts expect this regional market to retain its position over the forthcoming years.

projects.description:
Global Low Intensity Sweeteners Market: Snapshot

In the last few years the world has witnessed drastic change in lifestyle and eating pattern across most developed and developing nations. While this paradigm shift is steered by adverse effects of unhealthy living, it is here to stay as people look for an overall better standard of living. As cutting down sweet seems easier way of committing toward a healthy living, the prevailing environment is highly conducive to the growth of the global low intensity sweeteners market. Low intensity sweeteners are food additives that taste like sugar but do not contain the same amount of calories as compared to the latter.

Riding on back of the rising diabetic population worldwide and overall initiatives to reduce burdens of obesity, the demand for low intensity sweeteners has considerably risen. projects.description:
Global Cosmetic Ingredients Market: Snapshot

The global market for cosmetic ingredients has been growing at a steady pace, thanks to the escalating demand for cosmetic products across the world. The pursuit of beauty, together with the increasing consciousness of consumers towards physical appearance, and the rising awareness among them pertaining to skin care has fueled the demand for cosmetics substantially. Apart from this, the increasing trend of the anti-aging formulations is also driving the growth of this market.

On the flip side, the implementation of stringent government rules and regulations upon a number of ingredients is likely to act as a restraint in the growth trajectory of this market in the near future. However, the frequent and continual changes in the preferences of consumers are anticipated to generate lucrative opportunities for the progress of this market over the years to come. 

The global cosmetic ingredients market was worth US$22.89 bn in 2016 and is expected rise at a CAGR of 4.60% from 2017 to 2025, increasing to US$33.80 bn by the end of 2025.
Moisturizing Agents to Enjoy Continued High Demand

Cosmetic ingredients are mainly utilized as cleansing agents, moisturizing agents, and coloring agents. Among these, the moisturizing agents segment holds the most prominent share in this market, thanks to the extensive usage of moisturizing agents in skin care, hair care, and makeup cosmetics. Researchers anticipate the scenario to remain same over the next few years.

The demand for cleansing agents is also expected to increase considerably in the near future, especially in the skin care and hair care products. The growing awareness among consumers regarding the benefits offered by cleansing agents, such as effective removal of oil and dirt from skin and hair, is expected to influence their demand in the years to come.

projects.title: Honeycomb Packaging Market (Packaging Type - Interior Packaging, Exterior Packaging, and Pallets; End Use - Food & Beverage, Automotive Goods, Furniture, Consumer Goods, Industrial Goods, and Logistics Packaging) - Global Industry Analysis, Size, Share, G
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Transparency Market Research Pvt. Ltd.
projects.description:
The global market for honeycomb packaging is expected to expand at a considerable rate in the near future due to its growing demand across several industrial verticals. The increase application of honeycomb packaging and emphasis on environment-friendly packaging are two of the key drivers for te global honeycomb packaging market. As the demand for protective packaging grows in end-user industries such as consumer goods, automotive, and furniture among others, the honeycomb packaging market will witness significant expansion. In light of these reasons, the global honeycomb packaging market is expected to reach a valuation US$14.1 bn by the end of 2024 from US$8.6 bn in 2015. Between the forecast years of 2016 and 2024, the global market is projected to expand at a CAGR of 5.7%.

Honeycomb is gradually replacing bubble wrap, EPE, thermocol, EP foam, mineral wool, particle boards, rock wool, PUF, MDF, and wood in various packaging solutions. Thus, the rising focus on making packaging materials suitable to the environment and sustainable is expected to work in favour of the global market. Honeycomb packaging is gaining a strong foothold in a range of end-user industries that are in constant need of protective packaging. The report suggests that the emergence of e-commerce industry and the subsequent demand for transport of goods has provided the global market a phenomenal boost. This demand is largely a result of a need to protect damage and waste of items being shipped during transit.

On the basis of packaging type, the global honeycomb packaging market is segmented into interior packaging, exterior packaging, pallets and others. Exterior packaging held a dominant stance in the global market as of 2015 and is expected to do so in the coming years as well. Exterior packaging materials refer to the outer containers and boxes in which the products are packed before being shipped and transported.

projects.associatedWith: Associated with Transparency Market Research Pvt. Ltd.
projects.description:
In the global eyewear and eye care industries, the segment of contact lenses has witnessed a sweeping transformation from being once considered lifestyle products to common eye accessories sought as a convenient and fashionable replacement to glasses. The vast rise in product varieties and easy affordability of contact lenses have led to a vast rise in users of contact lenses or a regular basis these days.

Transparency Market Research estimates that the global contact lens market will expand at a healthy 7.6% CAGR over the period between 2016 and 2024. Expanding at this pace, the market, which had a valuation of US$9.74 bn in 2015 in terms of revenue, is projected to rise to US$18.70 bn by 2024. In terms of volume, the market is expected to rise to 2,135.0 mn units by 2024.

Cast Molding Emerges as Most Sought After Contact Lens Manufacturing Technology

Of the key technologies employed for manufacturing contact lenses, including spin casting, cast molding, and lathe cutting, cast molding is presently the most preferred technology. In 2015, the cast molding technology contributed a share of 80% in global market’s revenues. Owing to the automated and computer controlled production of contact lenses with the help of cast molding technology, the manufacturer is assured of accuracy and highest level of quality of the final product. Additionally, injection molding allows for bulk production of the extremely popular disposable lenses, making cast molding the preferred manufacturing modality for cost reductions.

headline: Healthcare IT
about:
Advocacy is opening up the room of requirements (Harry Potter reference).

From interacting with government officials to following up with a homeless patient in quarantine, the ubiquitous but not usually named skill of advocacy drives much of our professional lives. I love this skill so much that I have lived at the poverty level and paid too much money to well-established groups to demonstrate its powerful impact. I believe advocacy looks different for each person/group/organization, but for myself, it means producing an effective strategy to solving a stubborn problem.

My advocacy specialties include analyzing available data and asking subject matter experts the right questions. I have a four (fork) pronged approach for projects I have tackled, and right after these words, you will also know my secret sauce strategy:

-State the problem most crudely since this means you are most honest.
-Use your favorite search engine and look up the state/national/worldwide organization associated with the theme of the problem you are trying to solve.
-Look up news and the latest open access research articles that closely align with your problem.
-Reach out to subject matter experts and request an informational discussion BUT be sure to add value in some way to show appreciation. 

Many skills come into play that I have refined per my above strategy. These include recruiting, relationship building, effective communication, and mentoring peers and students. headline: U.S. CPA
about:
U.S. CPA (Washington State) and experienced tax professional with over 10 years of experience in U.S. tax advisory and compliance services, both in Japan and the United States. Currently working as a Manager at Deloitte Japan, I specialize in international tax compliance for Japanese financial institutions and multinational corporations, including QI (Qualified Intermediary) and FATCA regulations.

My career began in the legal field as a paralegal in the M&A team at a major law firm in Tokyo, where I developed my foundational skills in contract review, regulatory research, and cross-border transactions. I later transitioned into U.S. tax, supporting both corporate and individual clients—particularly expatriates and U.S. subsidiaries of Japanese companies—during my time at EOS Accountants LLP in Chicago.

I hold a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) in International Law from Waseda University, and I bring a unique combination of legal insight and tax technical expertise. I am passionate about helping Japanese clients navigate complex international tax landscapes. Currently on a career break for parenting, I am also preparing for a future overseas assignment and continually developing my English and global business communication skills.

publications.title: Eminent Need:  Proposing a Market Participant Exception for Municipal Parker Immunity
publications.publishedAt: Cardozo Public Law, Policy & Ethics Journal · Aug 1, 2011
publications.description: A township is using its eminent domain powers to become a monopsony in the real estate market for the designated area.  That township’s monopsony power is then being exploited to create a price-fixing scheme that would violate antitrust laws, either as a per se violation under § 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act, or as a monopolizing or attempted monopolizing offense under § 2.  Under the Sherman Act, effected residents could force the township to appraise each property individually and pay the full market value; if the township refused, they would be subject to the treble damage penalty, erasing any possible advantage of abusing its monopsony power.  As the law currently stands, however, a township is immune from suit under the Parker v. Brown decision, and its progeny.  This paper will use the real-life example of Mount Holly, New Jersey, and the story of one effected resident to illustrate the need for a market participant exception to Parker immunity, such that when a municipality is participating in the market for a good itself, as opposed to merely regulating that market, the Sherman Act should apply.

publications.title: International Coffee Regulation:  A Comparison of the International Organization and the Fair Trade Coffee Regimes
publications.publishedAt: Cardozo Public Law, Policy & Ethics Journal · Dec 1, 2008
publications.description:
7 Cardozo Pub. L. Pol'y & Ethics J. 2008

I examined 30 years of monthly coffee price data to determine that there is a trend of roughly ($0.0127)/month measured in 2007 U.S. dollars.  Coffee producers are being priced out of production. Unable to cover their own overhead, their national governments have attempted to regulate the world coffee market-efforts that have been consistently unsuccessful. Some farmers have turned to the alternative market for Fairtrade coffee, with its promises of higher prices. Fairtrade farmers voluntarily embrace higher costs and more intense labor, but the return
is indefinite at best.
Oversupply has caused the historical and current price crises facing struggling coffee farmers. This Note contends that only through embracing measures to reduce oversupply will producers be able to raise themselves from poverty. With the diversification of exporting economies, producers may now have options outside of production. It is the purpose of this Note to not merely illustrate the current state of international coffee regulation, but also to suggest that the market already has a solution: exit from production. Those who do so will be able to explore broader economic options. But the current regulatory regimes are geared towards keeping coffee farmers in production, with only minimal efforts to promote diversification and exit. Strategies to increase demand fail to address the problem underlying low prices, and oversupply will only be eliminated through producer exit, finally making coffee production viable for those who remain.

education.description:
The CAIA Charter is the globally recognized credential for professionals managing, analyzing, distributing, or regulating alternative investments. The CAIA Charter designation is the highest standard of achievement in alternative investment education and provides deep knowledge, demonstrated expertise, and global credibility in alternatives.

Established in 2002, the CAIA Charter is a comprehensive program comprised of a two-tier exam process through which a candidate may become a CAIA Charter Holder. The Level I exam assesses a candidate's understanding of various alternative asset classes and a candidate's knowledge of the tools and techniques used to evaluate the risk-return attributes of each one. The Level II exam assesses how a candidate would apply the knowledge and analytics learned in Level I within a portfolio management context. Both levels include segments on ethics and professional conduct.

about:
As a dedicated Tax Consultant at Deloitte Tax LLP in Chicago, I leverage my expertise to deliver exceptional results in complex tax matters. My journey in the field of accounting began at the University of Iowa, where I completed my Bachler's and Master's degree in Accounting. This rigorous academic background provided me with a solid foundation in accounting principles and practices.

What sets me apart in my role is not just my technical skills, but also my unwavering commitment to excellence. I am known for my meticulous attention to detail and my relentless pursuit of perfection. This translates into thorough, accurate, and reliable tax solutions for our clients.

In my tenure at Deloitte, I have had the opportunity to work on a variety of tax-related projects. These range from routine tax compliance to intricate tax planning and strategy. My approach is always client-centric, ensuring that their needs are at the forefront of every solution I provide.

Moreover, I am highly motivated and constantly seeking ways to improve processes and outcomes. I believe that continuous learning and adaptation are key to success in the ever-evolving field of tax consultancy. As such, I regularly engage in professional development opportunities to stay abreast of the latest trends and regulations in the industry.

I am excited about the future of tax consultancy and look forward to continuing to make significant contributions to the field and our clients.

about:
I’m a data leader with 7+ years of experience turning complex ideas into scalable, AI-powered products that generate ROI, uncover new revenue streams, and align technical development with business strategy.

I specialize in bridging the gap between innovation and execution—working across media, telecom, healthcare, defense, and government to build intelligent systems that make data actionable and valuable. Highlights include:
- Led teams to build agentic AI systems with custom agents that utilize RAGs
- Designed ETL pipelines that saved $60K/month and boosted model accuracy
- Created predictive models that improved hospital outcomes and reduced patient readmissions

At my core, I believe data is just the beginning. The real value comes from systems that are smart, strategic, and user-centered. I’ve presented technical ideas to C-level executives, mentored new practitioners, and traveled on-site to meet clients where they are—on factory floors, in data centers, or behind the whiteboard.

From deploying GenAI before playbooks existed to uncovering hidden growth in dashboards no one thought to build—I aim to build smart, ship fast, and deliver results that last.

Let’s connect if you're working on data strategy, applied AI, or building products that scale.

experience.description:
Working at Deloitte, I combine strategy with data science techniques to help clients envision and build solutions to keep up with the rapidly developing landscape of AI. 


• Managed a cross-functional team to develop an agentic AI system that generates personalized Outlook calendars and summarizes profiles for client trips, saving users 12+ hours of manual research through tailored recommendations and conflict detection.
• Led AI-driven initiatives to tackle complex governance challenges across professional services domains, including legal (ERISA), consulting (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA), finance (BEPS Pillar 2, Transfer Pricing), cybersecurity (ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2), tax (FATCA, BEPS, CRS), and audit (SEC, PCAOB, IFAC).
• Designed and implemented a virtual assistant, leveraging retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, and custom guardrails, that aggregates data from 9 sources and delivers concise, source-backed responses, achieving a 99.4% user satisfaction score.
• Engineered a regex-driven ETL pipeline to extract important fields, increasing feature availability by 25%, improving model accuracy, and enabling reusable workflows with stakeholder-friendly visualizations.
• Devised and applied advanced outlier removal and spoofing detection techniques, reducing data storage needs by 75%, accelerating runtime by 700%, and saving the client $60K per month for storage costs.
• Consolidated client data into a single cloud provider, saving the client $120k/month.
• Developed a pipeline using hex KD-tree clustering to transform geospatial data into trajectories, enabling rapid analysis of movement, important locations, and device co-location previously hidden in the data. 
• Partnered with account leads to develop technical solutions, contributing to $29M in new sales.

• Led a multidisciplinary team to build a scalable AWS infrastructure with Databricks for a 40+ hospitals system. Deployed a patient readmission prediction model that enabled real-time insights for doctors and improved outreach through personalized reminders for high-risk patients; reduced readmissions by 28%.
• Built systems that automated manual review processes, unified fragmented data sources, and integrated legal and trade associations’ educational materials, improving compliance accuracy to 99.7%.
• Routine speaker on effective team management for successful AI deployments. With the recent hype of ChatGPT, often educated stakeholders on differences between Generative AI and traditional AI algorithms.
• Led a model migration effort with a cross-functional team from an internal system to Databricks, shortening model run time by 2 hours and reducing complexities for data scientists and engineers on future projects.
• Created a healthcare optimization model to find the most desirable collection of initiatives that a healthcare plan can implement to improve their ratings for the following year, which reduced cost by 20%.
• Discovered errors in a pre-existing model for reducing wait times between shipment dates; once corrected, it reduced average wait time by 25%.

• Created analytical reports for the Executive team to forecast revenue and gauge the amount of new hires needed after acquiring an account with more than $500 million in potential premiums.
• Processed complex data sets dealing with the loss history of over 400 clients, which we used to uncover opportunities for specific risk-control opportunities.
• Responsible for uncovering areas where over 400 clients could use additional coverage.

•	Spearheaded an optimization analysis of promotional approval limits in order to more efficiently
distribute workload within the Sales Finance team. 
•	Helped manage the P&L for the Americas and assisted in forecasting a 5-year P&L for a new market. 
•	Checked and updated pricing and costs in SAP to ensure that there was not cross-channel conflict among different promotional events and retailers. 
•	Consolidated financial planning documents to make information more readily available.

•	Tested a new equity-trading gateway to make clients’ trades more efficient.
•	Discovered discrepancies in  financial reporting of clients' billings between departments.
•	Performed cost-saving analyses, created automated reports for tracking monthly trading volume by client to reveal which clients trade the most per year and per month.
•	Identified and consolidated protocols per exchange to streamline the process for cases when a client accidentally makes a trade.
•	Assisted a Senior Financial Advisor with client interactions, preparation of client proposals, asset allocations and portfolio construction.

publications.description:
...When I come to, I realize that everyone is being summoned for a happy little game of charades. I pour another glass of wine and head into the living room, trying diligently not to spill anything on the red and black rooster pillows, needlessly strewn about the room. I scan around for an open spot and ultimately sit on the couch.  Who sits next to me, but Chatty Cathy and her Chardonnay. “We should be teammates,” she says to me. I better answer her, “That’ll be grand.” It’s too early in the evening to be forcing conversation. Every single muscle in my body is clenched. I ponder how nice it would be to take a bath in muscle rub, but I’m just too young to reek of Ben-Gay. Someone (Chatty Cathy) decides it would be the best thing ever to play the soundtrack to Phantom or is it the score? Whichever one it is invokes a riotous conversation about Broadway and how fabulous the theatre is—maybe if you are a chair and you don’t have ears. Well, that’s not social at all. Look sharp soldier! The scenes are being distributed. I unfold a piece of paper with “Lassie” scribbled on it. Who knew the comedy troupe was in town? I consider whipping out my lighter, setting the carpet on fire, and barking at it. That would be rude. When my turn comes up, I get down on all fours and bark. How entertaining. Chatty Cathy gets it. She must be psychic. My watch tells me it’s time for another glass of wine. When I return, the game is still going strong. A man with not enough to do is eyeballing me. Oh, no. He must have taken my “dead eyes” to mean, “Hey, why don’t you come over and chat with me?”
(…More upon request)
